mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE drops below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS (payroll employment) and a fall in UNRATE over the same month indicates a labor market expansion without wage inflation pressure, which supports corporate profit growth and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both Real Final Sales (RSAFS) and Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where both RSAFS and HOUST decline by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month while FEDFUNDS remains unchanged, it signals insufficient monetary tightening to contain inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS is unchanged.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDPC1) of at least 2.5% signals robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where quarterly GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5%.
